purpose: small identity-preserving corrections; no runtime launch

requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: single whole-pose pixel-art sprite correction for Clockwork's existing IRON MAW mechanical four-legged guardian.
Input images: Image 1 is the specific existing game-pixel frame to EDIT. Image 2 is the stable existing native idle pose, identity and pixel-art style reference. Image 3 is the original canonical character design reference, identity/rigid mechanical construction only, NOT its smooth rendering style.
Keep the same navy-steel body, grey riveted upper and lower jaws, circular leg hinge housings, silver piston rods, three red back vents and red mouth machinery. Keep the original left-facing side/three-quarter camera, same recognizable head/body/leg proportions and grounded mechanical feet. Do not invent a new boss design, extra limbs, eyes, horns, weapons, tail, props or effects.
Style: crisp low-resolution hand-authored pixel clusters at the original game sprite density, flat hard-edged metal surfaces, dark 1-pixel outline, navy/grey/red palette, no soft gradients, no anti-aliasing, no texture noise, no smooth concept-art shading. This is a careful anatomy/rigid plate correction, not a restyle.
Output: exactly ONE isolated whole-body corrected pose, full silhouette and all feet visible, genuinely transparent background, no cast shadow or floor, no grid, labels, comparison panels or sprite sheet. Keep transparent margins around the complete sprite.
Mechanical constraint: metal plates are rigid; pose changes occur at circular hinge joints. Do not squash or stretch the head, jaw plates, body shell, pistons or individual legs. Reuse the same part sizes and connect pistons cleanly to their joint pivots.
Specific correction: Correct this neutral standing idle sprite very subtly: clarify straight jaw plate edges, align circular hinges, and reconnect the leg pistons cleanly. Preserve the exact stable stance, open red-lit mouth, compact body width, foot spacing, facing and overall silhouette of Image 1. This pose will be the fixed structural baseline for a subtle idle power pulse; do not add a breathing squash or move the head to a different angle.
